title: Letter order accepting Southwest Power Pool, Inc.'s 03/12/2026 filing of proposed revisions to Part I, section 1 and Attachment Z1 of its Open Access Transmission Tariff to provide Eligible Customers with flexibility etc. under ER26-1731.
entity: SECRETARY OF THE COMMISSION, FERC; SECRETARY OF THE COMMISSION, FERC; COMMISSIONERS AND IMMEDIATE STAFF (THE COMMISSION)

documents.text:
195 FERC ¶ 61,107
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
WASHINGTON, DC  20426

May 11, 2026


								In Reply Refer To:
Southwest Power Pool, Inc.
Docket No. ER26-1731-000
					
Southwest Power Pool, Inc.
201 Worthen Drive
Little Rock, AR  72223

Attention:  Meredith Powell

Dear Ms. Powell:

On March 12, 2026, Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (SPP) filed, pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act and Part 35 of the Commission’s regulations, proposed revisions to Part I, section 1 (Definitions) and Attachment Z1 (Aggregate Transmission Service Study and Cost Allocation and Recovery for Service Upgrades) of its Open Access Transmission Tariff (Tariff) to provide Eligible Customers with flexibility to procure Long-Term Service through the Aggregate Transmission Service Study (ATSS) process while seeking generator interconnection service through the applicable generator interconnection process.  As discussed below, we accept the proposed Tariff revisions, effective May 12, 2026, as requested.
SPP states that Attachment Z1 of the Tariff describes the ATSS process used to evaluate Long-Term Service requests and that, under the ATSS process, SPP combines all Long-Term Service requests during a specified period of time (open season) into a single ATSS, apart from certain requests that meet certain exemption requirements.  SPP states that combining all requests received during an open season allows SPP to develop  a more efficient expansion of the transmission system that provides the necessary Available Transfer Capability to accommodate all such requests at the minimum total cost.  SPP states that, during an open season, an Eligible Customer may request      Long-Term Service by submitting a Completed Application.
SPP states that its existing Business Practice 7500 expands on the Tariff’s requirements for the ATSS and limits the amount of Long-Term Service an Eligible Customer may request from a specific point of interconnection (POI) to the injection limit at the POI as determined by the Generator Interconnection Agreement(s) (GIA) associated with the POI.  SPP further explains that Business Practice 7500 allows SPP to reject any Long-Term Service request submitted into the ATSS process from resources at the same POI, which causes existing plus requested transmission service to exceed the GIA interconnection service amount at the POI.  SPP states that the purpose of the limitation is to minimize the risk of overselling system capacity, which could lead to unnecessary congestion and curtailment of service.  SPP further states that Business Practice 7500 allows an Eligible Customer to seek Long-Term Service and interconnection service simultaneously, thereby facilitating load additions and optimizing transmission usage.
SPP proposes to revise the Tariff to add these provisions from Business Practice 7500 into new section VII (Transmission Service Limit) in Attachment Z1 of the Tariff.  SPP states that the language of Business Practice 7500 should be documented in the Tariff and made part of the filed rate because the language affects the rates, terms, and conditions of SPP transmission service.  SPP asserts that the proposed revisions are just and reasonable and not unduly preferential or discriminatory because they allow SPP to manage and protect system capacity and offer Eligible Customers the flexibility to procure Long-Term Service through the ATSS while simultaneously seeking generator interconnection service.  SPP argues that the added flexibility will benefit Eligible Customers seeking service through both processes and will benefit SPP stakeholders and the footprint as a whole by facilitating load additions and optimizing transmission usage while minimizing the risk of overselling system capacity.
In addition, SPP proposes to add a new defined term, Point of Interconnection, to Part I, section 1 of the Tariff, which SPP proposes to define as:  “A physical location, as set forth in Appendix A to the Generator Interconnection Agreement, Interim Generator Interconnection Agreement, or Consolidated Planning Process Generator Interconnection Agreement (CPP GIA), as applicable, where the Interconnection Facilities connect to the Transmission System.”  SPP states that the newly defined term is necessary due to the proposed Tariff revisions in Attachment Z1 describing resource limitations at the POI.
Notice of SPP’s filing was published in the Federal Register, 91 Fed. Reg. 12791 (Mar. 17, 2026), with interventions and protests due on or before April 2, 2026.  Louisiana Public Service Commission filed a notice of intervention.  Timely motions to intervene were filed by:  Ameren Services Company, on behalf of its affiliate Union Electric Company; American Electric Power Service Corporation, on behalf of its affiliates Public Service Company of Oklahoma, Southwestern Electric Power Company, AEP Oklahoma Transmission Company, Inc., and AEP Southwestern Transmission Company, Inc.; Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company; and Sunflower Electric Power Corporation. 
Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure,        18 C.F.R. § 385.214 (2025), the notice of intervention and the timely, unopposed motions to intervene serve to make the entities that filed them parties to this proceeding.
We find the proposed Tariff revisions to be just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory or preferential and therefore accept them, effective May 12, 2026, as requested.  Specifically, we find that SPP’s proposed revision that allows SPP to refuse   a Long-Term Service request submitted into the ATSS process that results in existing transmission service plus the requested transmission service to exceed the interconnection limit at the POI is a reasonable limitation that will minimize the risk of overselling capacity on the transmission system, which in turn helps avoid unnecessary congestion 

and curtailment of service.  We also find that the proposed, new definition of Point of Interconnection provides clarity because it specifies the applicable location of the interconnection limits referenced in new section VII.
By direction of the Commission. 

						

Debbie-Anne A. Reese,
Secretary.
